content.comment_body: I have set up a message text to show the status of five flags (M1-M2-M3-M4-M5). The messages for M2-M3-M4-M5 are visible on the controller, but the one linked to M1 is missing from the controller display. When I connect online from my PC, I can see the M1 text correctly. If there were any software mismatches between the controller and PC, I would not be able to go online. Does anyone know the reason for this? Thanks. PS: I posted a video in a social media group to illustrate the issue better. Here is the link: [url]
A video hosted externally is not very useful. It's better to attach files within the forum, ideally sharing the project as a ZIP archive. Regards, [user_name]
I don't use social media, so I'm unable to view your video. Please upload your project file as a compressed package to the forum instead.

The video file is too large to attach. Photos show that bit M1 is ON. When online from the PC, the message window correctly shows Level 0 = OFF (since M1 = ON means the text should indicate OFF), but nothing appears on the controller itself. To remedy this, I deleted the text element and recreated it with a new block and numbering.

A similar issue was discussed in the German section of the forum recently: 'Message text is not displayed despite active block'. [company_name] support recommended rewriting the program in these cases; that's official guidance. According to their development department, this problem shouldn't occur when using [product_name] V[version_no], but whether that's reliable is questionable.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing inconsistencies with how message texts appear on the controller versus when viewed online from a PC. In particular, the message for the M1 flag does not show on the controller display, although other messages work as intended and the PC view is correct. Recreating message blocks seems to resolve the issue, and similar problems have been discussed in other forum sections, indicating this may be a software-related bug in message handling.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect message texts programmed for the system to be displayed the same way on both the controller and the PC when online, so that information is consistently communicated.
